In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

- The site binding is characterized by the existence of two types of site binding: - The "strong site binding" is characterized by the release of all or most of the electrostriction of the first hydration sphere and the loss of one water molecule.

- the site binding is a dynamic phenomenon, - the life time of the site binding depends on the counterion, on the nature of the polyelectrolys and on the concentration, - the site binding of a given counterion is not a single phenomenon but is composed of several different types, - the site bound counterion can be in two different types of sites, one of which corresponds to a loss of water molecules.
the site bound counterions are not in equilibrium with the bulk of the solution and that the site binding is not a reversible process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the counterion binding sites are not fixed on the polyelectro lyte chain but that the binding is dynamic and that the site binding is not a static phenomenon.
the site binding is a process of exchange between free and site bound states, the latter being a state of partial dehydration and partial electrostriction release.
the site bound counterions can be considered as "frozen" in a cage of water molecules and the relaxation of water protons is mainly due to the diffusion of this cage in the solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the water protons chemical shift in these systems is not a good indicator of the site binding process, whereas the relaxation times are.
the water protons chemical shift and the water proton relaxation time measurements on polyelectrolys solutions are very sensitive to the existence of site binding and to its characteristics.
site binding can be described as a dynamic equilibrium between free and bound counterions.
